label: HOST_ORACLE_VISUAL_FEASIBILITY
kind: DIAGNOSTIC. Explains why the with_floor variant is degenerate and must not be read as a result.

the_degenerate_numbers.why_they_are_not_a_100_percent_recall: the Delta-E series is identically zero, so the 90th-percentile threshold is 0.0 and every frame trivially 'exceeds' it. This is a divide-by-degenerate artefact, not a perfect carrier. Read only the without_floor variant, which the pre-registration named primary before any score existed.

mechanism_measured.test: render a C major triad and an F major triad through the identical pipeline under both weightings
mechanism_measured.reading: bloom_chromagram's [0.65, 1.0] floor alone shrinks the C-to-F colour distance by about 4x (0.289 -> 0.0735). The existing HOST preview exposure of 2.2 then saturates BOTH chords to pure white. Two different chords become the same pixel.

honest_caveats: exposure 2.2 is the lab's HOST PREVIEW transform, not the device display, so the final saturation step is a preview property
even without any exposure the floor still removes ~75% of the colour separation, so the floor is the dominant mechanism, not the preview
this sandbox is not the compiled bloom engine; it reuses bloom's documented chromagram semantics (hue b/12, weight = squared drive), not its binary

what_this_supports.why: the compatibility pin already warns 'Product palette path (K1_Ultraviolet_Bright, chromatic_mode=false) made hue_centroid a weak HOST observable. Do not treat palette-locked hue as a chroma test.' This is that warning measured: under the product-faithful drive, a real chord change produces a Delta-E of exactly zero.
what_this_supports.what_it_is_NOT: evidence that harmonic information lacks visual value. The same information under an unfloored mix produces Delta-E 44.1 on the same chord change. The constraint is in L6/L7, not in the perception.
